title: an install inspector and gate
intention: A box's install is measured, not remembered. Recovery's bootstrap brings up python and the venv only. One install-inspector call measures every other install fact and reds each lack, and an install gate, asked rather than called, refuses to call the box installed while any red stands.
why: Akien, 2026-11-12, verbatim: "i would say we need an install inspector and gate. then we can set up python, and once it's set up use that to detect what else with just a tool call. part of recovery and install". Measured the same day: akienasus had none of the 15 skills and no pytest, akiendell none of the 16 skills, and each was fixed by hand, because a box gets only what someone remembered to add and nothing reads what is missing.
traces_to: Law 3: an install is not known until measured. Law 4: install facts are enforced by an inspector and gate, not remembered. Law 1: each hand-fix becomes a registered check.
how: inspector.py in Recovery: CHECKS lists 'module:function' step functions shaped {id,status,detail}; inspect() runs each with dry_run=True and reds every status but already_applied (a raise is a red); installed() returns (ok, reds). installer.main() becomes ask_cairn_home and ask_box_identity (human questions, outside CHECKS), then inspect, then fix_reds(checks) over the reds with dry_run=False, then ask installed(), exiting 0 only when it is ok; --check prints the reds and writes nothing. Children prove first: ce1d61032eff (the move), b3ecebdf9695 (dev extra, re-shaped into a check). 53e7979f76e7 (skill links) registers ensure_skill_links into CHECKS when it lands. The commons root joins when akiendell_cc_0 casts its resolver.

clauses.claim: with one green, one offered and one raising check, inspect() returns exactly two reds naming their lacks, the raising one carrying its exception
installed() is (False, those reds) while any red stands and (True, []) once all are green
inspect() calls every check with dry_run=True and writes nothing; a scratch repo's git config is byte-identical after it measures ensure_journal_merge_driver
the install run calls each red check once with dry_run=False and no green check, then asks installed() again

decisions.text: D1: inspector.py holds CHECKS (module:function strings), inspect(checks=None) -> list[dict], and installed(checks=None) -> tuple[bool, list[dict]]. A check is a 'module:function' string or a callable (functools.partial included), so a proof can aim one at a scratch repo. A check returning a list (the host-seam install()) yields one entry per item. The first CHECKS are the installer's install, ensure_journal_merge_driver and ensure_dev_extra. Only checks that exist are registered: ensure_skill_links is built by ticket 53e7979f76e7, which registers it into CHECKS when it lands.
D2: the new component's charter, written before BUILDME through the artifact door: it is Recovery's machine, its public_interface is inspect/installed/CHECKS, and its why is Akien's words verbatim.

D3: the named seam fix_reds(checks=None, *, run_checks=None) -> list[dict] in the installer, which main() calls: it inspects, then calls each red check once with dry_run=False and no green check, and returns their results. ask_cairn_home and ask_box_identity stay outside CHECKS: they ask the human, and the gate measures the box. Clause 4's tooth drives fix_reds with fake checks.

D4: installer.main() (at its post-ce1d61032eff address) runs ask_cairn_home and ask_box_identity, then inspect, then fix_reds over the reds, then installed(); --check prints the reds and exits 1 if any stand. bin/cmd/install passes --check through unchanged.
D5: the proof drives injected fake checks and the real ensure_journal_merge_driver over a scratch git repo, one tooth per clause (PROVES 1-4).

out: each check's own logic (its child's ticket)

measured.saw: akienasus had 0 of 15 skills and no pytest; akiendell 0 of 16 skills; each fixed by hand
measured.how: orchestrator's relay of the two boxes' CC reports

measured.saw: every installer step already returns {id,status,detail} and has a dry_run that writes nothing

A spawn's interpreter must import the parent's packages. cairn.tools.windowless_spawn.background_python() returned the base interpreter (sys.prefix C:\Users\akien\AppData\Local\Python\pythoncore-3.14-64), not the venv (C:\Users\akien\.cairn\venv); a child spawned through it died at import psycopg2 (ModuleNotFoundError, bus.log) while the venv itself imports psycopg2 2.9.13. Fixed in bfbfe42a7; its tooth 1 now compares the child's sys.prefix to the parent's. An install check could catch the class: a spawn interpreter whose site-packages differ from the caller's. The spawn-interpreter install check is the follow-up ticket 404f193284ac, not part of this one.
measured.how: background_python() run with -c 'import sys; print(sys.prefix)' and compared with the venv's sys.prefix; bus.log tail; python -c 'import psycopg2' in the venv python

orient.intent: One inspect() call measures every registered install fact with dry_run=True and reds each lack; installed() is the gate that refuses while a red stands; the installer's fix_reds calls each red once with dry_run=False.
orient.scope: install_inspector/inspector.py, fix_reds and the main() rewiring in installer.py, and one proof; skill-link checks (53e7979f76e7), the spawn-interpreter check (404f193284ac), bootstrap.sh and the commons root are out

constraints.text: Nothing enters proven-space without a proof a hollow build couldn't pass.
Errors are loud at diagnostic surfaces and permanent in records of truth: a raising check is a red, never swallowed.
every component talks to every other only through its public interface
